summary: Douglas County site: 1934 40-foot L-4 tower, storm-destroyed 1962 and rebuilt 1963, discontinued 1975; no source describes what remains on the butte today.

facts.design: 40-foot L-4 cab on the 1934 tower; timber tower with ODF cab rebuilt in 1963 (40 or 41 feet by source)
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the October 1962 storm and rebuilt in 1963; discontinued in 1975; tower gone by 1975; parts salvaged 1976; no source describes the site today

staffing.status: fire-season lookouts in the sources read, last named staffing 1948; discontinued 1975

events.note: Planned as a primary lookout point serving the Eastern and Western Lane County and Douglas County fire patrol associations (The Forest Log, September 1, 1933)
40-foot L-4 lookout tower built; a CCC camp completed a road to the top of the butte in August 1934
George Fisher took over the lookout for the remainder of the 1934 fire season
A woman in charge of the lookout station for the Douglas Forest Protective association
Wanda Harden to remain at the lookout for the summer months as a forest fire lookout
New aluminum roof put on at a cost of $416.37
Destroyed by heavy winds in the Columbus Day storm, October 12, 1962; state restoration funds paid $4,000 of the $5,545 rebuild (see 1963)
Replacement timber tower with cab built at a cost of $5,545, of which $4,000 came from the state restoration fund; 40 feet per Forest Lookouts, 41 feet per firetower.org and firelookout.com
Lookout discontinued (Forest Lookouts); tower removed by 1975 (firetower.org) or destroyed by 1975 (firelookout.com)
Lookout dismantled and parts salvaged for the new Mt. Scott lookout
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register as US 932, OR 290

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives the 1963 tower as 40 feet; firetower.org and firelookout.com give 41 feet. The story says the sources differ and gives no single figure.
firelookout.com says about 8 miles southwest; the 1940 survey datasheet quoted on Forest Lookouts says 7.0 miles. The story gives a range.
firetower.org and firelookout.com call the 1962 event the Columbus Day hurricane; Forest Lookouts calls it the Columbus Day storm. It is the same event, and the story uses storm.

notes_for_editor: Gone site. The current status and site condition are not described by any source read; a WebSearch turned up only old pages and a topo map with no lookout detail. The brief's 12.2 m height matches the 1934 40-foot tower, not the 1963 replacement, so the story says sources differ on the replacement. Gone by 1975 per firetower.org and firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts says discontinued 1975 and dismantled 1976. Story and quotes avoid the names of private people in the 1936 wedding and 1957 snake items, which are left out. Reads: firetower.org (1), firelookout.com (1), Forest Lookouts (1); one WebSearch. Photos: none new in the pages read.
